newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan vegoil rates seen stable on new imports.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan vegoil rates seen stable on new imports.

text.p: Pakistani vegetable oil rates are likely to remain stable next week on new imports and plentiful stocks, dealers said on Saturday.
"Four ships with vegoil are due this month, while we have over 133,000 of unsold vegoil stocks," said dealer Mohammad Kamran of Saulat Enterprises.
Rumours that duty on vegoil imports would be reduced in Friday's budget for fiscal 1997/98 (July-June) proved incorrect.
"Buyers were sidelined before the budget on hopes of duty cuts, but as the post-budget picture is now clear, we expect demand to rise," he said.

Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said in his budget speech 2.2 million hectares of land would be brought under canola, mustard and sunflower cultivation to produce 400,000 tonnes of edible oil and 750,000 tonnes of oilcakes and save foreign exchange.
Saulat Enterprises said four ships with more than 84,000 tonnes of vegoil were due this month, while arrival of local supplies would pick up in the next few weeks.
Vegoil stocks fell to around 133,000 tonnes from 145,000 tonnes on June 6.
